codeReview.summary: The feature adds `sentry-sdk`, introduces `python/core/sentry.py`, and wires `init_sentry()` / `flush_sentry()` into the three files named in the feature description. However, the actual workflow subprocess entry point that the server launches is still `python/runners/run_workflow.py`, and that script was left without direct Sentry init/flush at its process boundary, so workflow startup and import-time failures can still escape Sentry capture.

issues.description: `run_workflow.py` remains the real workflow runner entry point (`server/api/workflows.ts:20,242` spawns it), but this feature did not add `init_sentry()` / `flush_sentry()` there. The script still just does `setup_logging(); raise SystemExit(main())`, so Sentry is only initialized later inside the imported `python.runners.workflow.entrypoint.main()`. Any failures during `run_workflow.py` startup or top-level imports happen before Sentry is active, which leaves the workflow runner incompletely covered by the integration.

summary: Reviewed the handoff, transcript skeleton, skill, and commit `0d3d8a5`. I marked the feature as failing because the true workflow subprocess wrapper, `python/runners/run_workflow.py`, was not instrumented directly, leaving workflow startup/import failures outside Sentry coverage; I also noted shared-state mismatches around entry-point documentation and skill-procedure tracking.
